$comment: Root ADR-0619. The base of the AWS account the data jobs move to (root ADR-0616): which account, which region, the tags every resource carries, the state bucket, the account's monthly budget, the network, and Dagster's place: its cluster, service, database and alarm (root ADR-0616 A1). infra/aws/main.tf reads this file and nothing else decides these values; the provider refuses every other account (allowed_account_ids), so an apply under the wrong profile stops before it reads or changes anything. Applied from the laptop with the SSO profile after the PR merges (docs/runbooks/aws-platform.md); nothing applies it on the data host.

account.name: perfectory-platform-prod
account.reason: The organization's platform account (made 2026-11-09 for the Seoul front door, root ADR-0461). The management account and the old gongzzang production account are never targets: they are not listed here, so the provider refuses them.

state.reason: The state of an AWS stack lives in its own account: the SSO role that applies it reads and writes it, so no second credential (the R2 keys the host's stacks use) reaches the laptop. Versioned so an apply that went wrong can be rolled back to the earlier state; old versions leave after 90 days. Locked by the S3 backend's own lock file (use_lockfile). The state holds no secret: the master password is RDS's own (manage_master_user_password) and the Dagster role's is written write-only (secret_string_wo); the state holds only the secrets' ARNs.

budget.name: perfectory-platform-monthly
budget.reason: Owner approval 2026-11-25: collection on AWS at about 92 USD a month on ARM, 160 in a month with a bulk collection (root ADR-0616 §10, re-stated at Fargate ARM prices). Actual spend past 100 is the first notice, past 150 the second; a forecast past 150 tells before the month ends. The budget mails the account's own registered address (a variable at apply time, never committed: this repository is public); budget mail needs no confirmation. Budgets without actions cost nothing.

network.address_reason: The VPC's own address block is given at apply time (TF_VAR_vpc_cidr), not written here: this repository is public and holds no private network addressing (scripts/guard/public-repository-safety.sh). This file decides the shape: a /16 cut into /20 subnets, each subnet the netnum its zone has in public_subnets or private_subnets (cidrsubnet). Once the VPC exists the runbook reads its block back from AWS, and the VPC and its subnets refuse to be destroyed (prevent_destroy), so a wrong block stops the plan instead of replacing the network.
network.reason: No NAT gateway and no load balancer (root ADR-0616 §1, §10). Tasks run in the public subnets with a public IPv4 address and no inbound rule: they reach the sources, R2, GHCR and the AWS APIs through the internet gateway. The private subnets have no route out and hold only the database (RDS needs subnets in two zones). Two zones, because RDS requires them; 2a and 2c because every Fargate and RDS class is offered there. The account's default VPC is left as it is and used by nothing here.

ecs.reason: One cluster for the Dagster service and every run task it launches (root ADR-0616 §1-§2). Container Insights stays off: the alarm reads the service metrics ECS publishes for free. Every role a run task may carry (the default run role with no policy, the run execution role, each lane's role) is under run_role_path, and Dagster may pass a role under that path and no other.

dagster.reason: Owner approval 2026-11-25 (root ADR-0616 A1): the webserver and the daemon in one always-on Fargate ARM task of 0.5 vCPU and 2 GB (on ai-server the three containers use 687 MiB together). The image is the release's AWS code location by digest (root ADR-0620), given at apply time; the workspace is the AWS code location, which holds no job until A2 moves collectors one at a time. Runs are tasks of their own (EcsRunLauncher), sized per run. No inbound rule and no public address of its own beyond the task's IPv4 for egress; the UI is reached by SSM port forwarding (ECS Exec). EcsRunLauncher registers every run's task definition in the family <run_task_definition_prefix>_<hashes> (dagster-aws get_task_definition_family; dagster-aws 0.29.27 refuses a prefix over 16 characters when it builds the launcher), and Dagster's role may start only that family: never the database bootstrap, which carries the master user's secret.

database.name: dagster

foundation.name: foundation
foundation.reason: The Bronze ledger's place (root ADR-0616 A1b, coordinator 2026-11-26): the data host's foundation schema on this instance, made by the same sqlx migrations (foundation-migrate from the release's arm64 runtime image), empty until a collector moves in (A2). The role names are the ones the migrations and infra/compose/grant-foundation-runtime.sql name (the runtime role is the one the collectors connect as on the data host). The migrator owns the schema; the runtime role reads and writes rows; each has its own secret, written write-only. Every rollout runs bootstrap, migrate, grants and finalize before the service moves (infra/aws/pre-deploy.sh).

database.reason: Dagster's storage (runs, events, schedules; 1,001 MB on ai-server) on RDS PostgreSQL, one zone, the smallest Graviton class (root ADR-0616 §1, §10: 18.25 USD a month plus 0.131 a GB). The disk grows by itself up to max_allocated_storage_gb (RDS storage autoscaling, no cost until it grows; at the ceiling 13.1 USD a month): on ai-server the ledger's schema `catalog` is 527 MB and Dagster's storage 1,001 MB (measured 2026-11-26). In the private subnets only, reached from the tasks' security group only, TLS required (PostgreSQL 15+ on RDS forces SSL by default). Least privilege: Dagster and every run task connect as app_username, a role that owns only this database, with its own secret (app_secret, in the shape Secrets Manager's RDS rotation reads; the password is written write-only, never in the state). The master user (master_username, its password RDS's own in Secrets Manager) is read only by the one-off bootstrap task that creates that role (infra/aws/database-bootstrap.sql). The Bronze ledger has its own database on this instance (foundation). Deletion protection and a final snapshot, so neither an apply nor a mistaken delete removes it.

chatbot.reason: AWS Chatbot (Amazon Q Developer in chat applications) has its control plane in four Regions (us-east-2, us-west-2, ap-southeast-1, eu-west-1), none of them ap-northeast-2, and its console in us-east-2 only. The channel configuration is managed through us-east-2; the topic and the alarms stay in the account's Region (one configuration takes topics of any Region). The service stores its configurations in those four Regions and may process a notification in any of them.

alarms.reason: Every alarm of this account publishes to one SNS topic. Urgent alarms go to Slack (owner, 2026-11-20) through AWS Chatbot (owner, 2026-11-26): the topic is bound to one Slack channel and no token or webhook is stored. Which alarms reach Slack is which alarms publish to the topic, in code (first: Dagster not running). The owner authorizes the Slack workspace once in the console; the workspace and channel ids are apply-time variables, not in this public repository.
